evidence.text: ___ yo F with a history of autoimmune hepatitis and cirrhosis c/b

___ s/p RFA and variceal bleed s/p banding, listed for liver 
transplant, who is transferred from ___ with embolic 
stroke and worsening portal vein thrombus.

Per report of patient's husband, she was in her usual state of 
health until ___, when he noted she was more quiet than usual 
during dinner and was having memory issues.

The following day, 
she had more difficulty with her speech, was not making complete 
sense and had some word finding difficulties.

Her blood pressure on 
arrival was 200/106 with a heart rate of 56.

Head CT showed a 
hypodensity in the left frontal and insula suggestive of a 
subacute infarct.
MRI/MRA of head and neck were notable for

"multiple small embolic infarcts within the left MCA territory, 
a small focal acute stroke within the right lateral cerebellar 
hemisphere, consistent with embolic infarcts from a central 
source." There was no evidence of significant stenosis within 
the anterior neck circulation and "hypoplastic left vertebral 
artery with possible area of stenosis within the proximal and 
mid segment." TTE with bubble study was negative for thrombus, 
aneurysm, areas of wall motion abnormality and shunt.

In 
addition, a CT abd/pelvis was notable for a "non-occlusive 
filling defect within the superior mesenteric vein extending to 
the confluence with the splenic vein extending into the portal 
vein consistent with nonocclusive thrombus." Notably patient was 
in sinus bradycardia throughout the hospitalization.

She was 
transferred to ___ for further 
management and decision regarding anticoagulation.

At the time of transfer, patient was hemodynamically stable, 
alert and oriented, with ongoing word finding difficulty, but 
ambulating without motor deficits.
On arrival to ___, vitals were 98.0F, 136/76, p55, RR18,

She says she 
has had some vision changes in the past few weeks, but unable to 
describe it.
No current blurry or double vision.

Patient 
continues to have very mild word finding difficulties and slowed 
speech.

ROS: per HPI, denies fever, chills, headache, cough, shortness 
of breath, chest pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, 
hematemesis, diarrhea, constipation, melena, hematochezia, 
dysuria, hematuria.
--c/b variceal bleed s/p banding in ___ and re-banding
--c/b HCC in left lobe s/p RFA c/b pneumothorax s/p chest tube

--listed for transplant on ___, MELD score 22 given 
exception points for HCC
# s/p TAH and USO for "abnormal cells"
No FHx bleeding problems or liver disease.

General- Pleasant slender elderly woman in bed in no acute 
distress.

Oral pharynx clear 
without erythema or exudates.
Abdomen- Normal bowel sounds, soft, nontender, nondistended.
Ext- No cyanosis, clubbing, or peripheral edema.

No stigmata of chronic liver disease 
including telangiectasias, spider angiomata, caput medusae, or 
palmar erythema.
Alert and oriented to person, place, time, hospital, president.

Can name objects throughout room, including clock, sheets, 
television, paper.
Can spell WORLD forward, but not backward.

Strength ___ upper extremities 
and ___ lower extremities.

Sensation to light touch in intact 
throughout.

Reflexes 1+ in biceps, triceps, and BR. 2+ patellar 
reflexes.
Speech for fluid without as much word finding difficulty.
POTASSIUM-4.0 CHLORIDE-105 TOTAL CO2-28 ANION GAP-8

___ EGD- 2 cords of grade II varices and 1 cord of grade I 
varices were seen in the lower third of the esophagus. 2 bands 
were successfully placed.

Erythema and mosaic appearance of the 
mucosa were noted in the antrum and stomach body.

These findings 
are compatible with Portal Hypertensive Gastropathy.

2. There is a hypodensity in the left frontal lobe and insula 
which is suggestive of a subacute infarct.
Anterior, middle and posterior cerebral arteries are nromal.

Basilar artery, intracranial carotids, 
and distal vertebral arteries are normal.

There are multiple small embolic infarcts within the left MCA 
territory involving the left frontal gray and white matter.

A 
more confluent area of infarct involves the left basal ganglia 
and subinsular region.

There is a small focal acute stroke 
wtihin the right lateral cerebellar hemisphere.

Conclusion- Acute infarcts within the left MCA territory and 
within the right posterior circulation.

Imaging findings are 
consistent with embolic infarcts from central source.

1. No evidence of significant stenosis within the anterior 
circulation.

2. Hypoplastic left vertebral artery with possible area of 
stenoses within the proximal and mid segment.
- LVEF 55% with mild LVH, normal contractility.

T wave 
inversions in V4-V6, nonspecific T wave changes in II, III, avF
1. There is no acute abnormality identified within the chest.

Specifically there is no evidence of metastatic disease within 
the chest.

3. There is a nodular contour of the liver with a shrunken 
appearance and heterogeneous coarse attenuation.

These findings 
raise the possibility of cirrhosis.

4. There is nonocclusive filling defect identified within the 
superior mesenteric vein extending to the confluence with the 
splenic vein extending into the portal vein consistent with a 
nonocclusive thrombus.

5. Spleen is enlarged with peripheral areas of lower attenuation 
which are nonspecific and may be sequela of previous insult 
though peripheral splenic infarcts cannot be excluded.

There is 
prominence of the main portal vein.

Overall these findings are 
suggestive of portal hypertension.

6. There is a mild amount of perihepatic ascites and ascites 
identified within the mesentery of the abdomen and lower pelvis 
consistent with polycystic kidney disease.
MCV-103* MCH-35.9* MCHC-34.8 RDW-14.6 Plt Ct-58*
1)There is no sign of pulmonary embolism thrombus formation.

There are no filling defects in the aorta or in the cardiac 
chambers.
Aorta and pulmonary arteries are normal in size.
3) There are no new lung nodules or pleural effusion.

___ F with autoimmune hepatitis and cirrhosis c/b ___ s/p RFA 
and variceal bleed s/p banding, transferred from ___ 
with embolic stroke and worsening portal vein thrombus.

# Embolic stroke - Only neurologic deficit despite multiple 
emboli on head MRI was word finding difficulty.

She had no 
motor, sensory or cranial nerve deficits.

Patient had extensive work-up at ___ as to the 
underlying etiology of stroke which was notable for no 
intracardiac thrombus, no significant carotid artery 
atherosclerosis or narrowing, and a TTE negative for PFO with 
bubble study.

At ___, she was also noted to be in sinus rhythm 
throughout hospitalization and cardiac CT did not note any 
thrombus or areas prone to thrombus formation within the heart.

However, given patient's portal vein thrombus and unclear 
etiology of embolic stroke, decision was made to anticoagulate, 
once there was evidence that prior varices were resolving.

At the time of 
discharge, expressive aphasia was improving, ___

# Portal vein thrombus- Patient had known partial left portal 
vein thrombus seen on CT scan ___, with extension of the 
thrombus into SMV and splenic vein on imaging at ___

As above, she has now been anticoagulated to prevent 
further progression of thrombus.

# Autoimmune hepatitis with cirrhosis- Patient listed for liver 
transplant on ___ with MELD of 22 (exception points for ___).

Complications of her cirrhosis include variceal bleed s/p 
banding and ___ s/p RFA.

There is no evidence of ___ recurrence 
or metastasis on CT thorax.

No history of ascites, coagulopathy, 
or hepatic encephalopathy.

She was continued on azathioprine and 
prednisone.

# Esophageal varices, hx of variceal bleeding- Last EGD ___ 
showed grade II varices which were banded without evidence of 
active bleeding.

EGD during this admission shows that varices 
are now grade I. HR at goal 50-60 on nadolol 40mg daily which 
was continued.
# Hypertension- Continued home lisinopril and nadolol.
The Preadmission Medication list is accurate and complete.
Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
1)There is no sign of pulmonary embolism thrombus formation.
There are no filling defects in the aorta or in the cardiac chambers.
Aorta and pulmonary arteries are normal in size.
3) There are no new lung nodules or pleural effusion.

Speech/Swallowing: 1 order(s) before T_pa; first on hospital day 1, most recent 93.4 h before T_pa.
